events.title: JavaScript standardized
events.summary: In June 1997, Ecma adopted the first official standard for JavaScript — giving Netscape JavaScript and Microsoft JScript one shared rulebook.
events.about: ECMAScript is the official name for the language inside every browser. This first standard meant web developers could write scripts expecting the same syntax in Netscape and Internet Explorer — the foundation for every modern web app, from form validation to single-page applications.

narrative.whyChosen: Standardization turned a browser-company invention into a written contract that any browser maker could implement.
narrative.whyImportant: It let JavaScript survive beyond Netscape and become the open web's programming language.
narrative.problemSolved: Without a standard, each browser vendor could change the language and break websites — the open web needed a stable definition.

sources.title: ECMA-262 1st edition — adopted by Ecma General Assembly June 1997
